clue.text: Removes protection for privates and retrieves mission data

blocks.note: first meaning, read jokily: takes off one's underpants, DE- plus briefs
second meaning: questions someone after an operation

explanation.surface: A soldier being stripped of kit and then questioned about the operation just completed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the word as DE (remove) + BRIEFS (underpants, which protect the 'privates', a pun on soldiers).
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief is to question an agent or soldier after an assignment to gather information.

clue.text: Unravel mystery of sea creature existing in freshwater river?

indicators.note: something existing in a place lives inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the Dee, a river in Britain; freshwater is surface colour
a cod is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a sea creature could be living in a freshwater river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England; 'freshwater' just adds to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode is to work out the meaning of something hidden, so solving a mystery.

clue.text: Arrogant supporter on way to enlightenment

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting garment
Zen Buddhism, a path to enlightenment

explanation.surface: A self-important backer who claims to be on the path to spiritual awakening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' is a crossword favourite for the garment, not a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazen means shameless and bold, which overlaps with arrogant behaviour.

clue.text: Apathy turning to defiance if son replaces daughter

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means a letter is swapped out for a new one

blocks.note: insolence is rude defiance
S is the abbreviation for son
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A sulky teenager's indifference becoming open rebellion when a son takes a daughter's place.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: the answer becomes the word for defiance when S replaces D, so the solver swaps D back in for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolence is laziness, an unwillingness to exert oneself, which is close to apathy.

clue.text: Spurned, I fail badly; did I  mean to say that?

definitions.text: did I  mean to say that?

indicators.note: badly suggests the words are put together wrongly, in a muddled order

blocks.note: as written
as written
as written

explanation.surface: A rejected suitor fumbling words and wondering whether a blurted remark was intended.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freudian slip is an accidental verbal error thought to reveal a hidden wish, so the speaker may have meant it.

clue.text: Extremely haughty getting put into elite category

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its two end letters only
something put into another word sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a plum job or role is a choice, elite one
first and last letters of haughty

explanation.surface: A very snooty person being admitted into a top-tier social group.
explanation.definitionFit: A phylum is a major rank in biological classification, so a taxonomic category.

clue.text: Couple pull up with difficulty?

blocks.note: first meaning: to attach, as a trailer to a car
second meaning: to hoist, as one does trousers
third meaning: a snag or problem

explanation.surface: A pair struggling to haul something upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to fasten, to jerk upward, and a temporary obstacle or snag.

clue.text: Circuit put on copier – it keeps the end clean

blocks.note: a loop is a circuit
an aper is one who apes, a copier

explanation.surface: Office instructions for loading a photocopier so the output stays tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copier' wants to be the office machine; it is one who apes. 'The end' means the backside, and LOO is the British word for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet tissue is used for wiping the bottom, the rear end of the body.

clue.text: Encounters rebel king's army chiefs inside – they're watchful creatures

indicators.note: chiefs are heads, so only the leading letter of each word is kept
inside means placed within, so one set of letters goes into the other word

blocks.note: meets, encounters
first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Meeting a rebel king's commanders, who keep a sharp lookout.
explanation.definitionFit: Meerkats are African mongooses famous for standing upright on sentry duty, keeping watch for predators.

clue.text: Caught dealer supplying 1/6th of friends in New York?

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a handler deals with or trades in goods

explanation.surface: A drug dealer arrested for supplying a group of friends in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'Friends' as the US sitcom set in New York: Chandler Bing is one of its six main characters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chandler Bing is one of the six title characters of the sitcom Friends, so a sixth of that group.

clue.text: Type of light half of street order

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word keeps three letters, here its opening part

blocks.note: the first three of six letters
the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: Someone asking what kind of lamp half the street has been told to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is the Order of the British Empire, a British honour, so 'order' gives those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a flashing lamp giving rapid bursts of light, as used in clubs.

clue.text: Adds all of raw mixture to make a healthy dish

indicators.note: a mixture combines things in a jumbled way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: as written
as written
as written
as written

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: combine all the raw ingredients for a wholesome meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This salad of apple, celery and walnuts in mayonnaise, from New York's Waldorf hotel, is a light dish.

clue.text: Live and thrive, having lost nothing

indicators.note: having lost something means a part is dropped from the phrase before it

blocks.note: to thrive is to do well
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Advice to live a full life and prosper, having lost nothing along the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live there, reside.

clue.text: Ask the mad criminal for final impression

indicators.note: criminal suggests the words are bent out of shape, made crooked

blocks.note: as written
as written
as written

explanation.surface: A detective deciding to quiz a deranged crook for a last impression of the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'criminal' does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A death mask is a cast taken of a face after death, literally a last impression.

clue.text: Brilliant old American lineage

blocks.note: of the Inca, the pre-Columbian people of Peru
ancestry, lineage

explanation.surface: Someone praising a person's brilliant ancestry from early American stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent means glowing with light, so brilliant in the sense of shining brightly.

clue.text: Strips back process, putting it into standby

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the word for strips is read the other way

blocks.note: to peel is to strip off
a mode is a way or method of operating

explanation.surface: Instructions for removing a backing and putting a gadget on standby.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleep mode is a low-power state of a computer, the setting also called standby.

clue.text: Cleaner is master, generating great presence

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
as written
MA, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A cleaner who becomes the boss and acquires a commanding personality.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British word for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is compelling personal charm, the quality of a strong presence that draws others.

clue.text: Dull recording broadcast by one of our cousins

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard on air, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: grey is dull, tape a recording

explanation.surface: A boring recording being aired by a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimps and orangutans are close evolutionary relatives of humans, hence our cousins.

clue.text: Alternative theatres rely on getting specialist treatment here?

indicators.note: alternative suggests a different version, so the words are rearranged

blocks.note: as written
as written

explanation.surface: Fringe theatres depending on special handling, a comment on arts funding.
explanation.walkthrough: Harley Street is the London street famous for private medical specialists; 'theatres' also hints at operating theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street is known for consultants in private practice, where patients go to see specialist doctors.

clue.text: Prone to prosecute, hiding fix

indicators.note: hiding something means wrapping it out of sight, so one word encloses another

blocks.note: to sue is to take legal action
to pin is to fix in place

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to take legal action while covering up a rigged result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone to' reads as 'inclined to', but 'Prone' is the definition and 'to' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe lying flat, though strictly supine is face upward and prone face down.

clue.text: Elevation moving top to bottom, 12.5%

indicators.note: moving the top of a down entry to its bottom shifts one letter from one end to the other

blocks.note: 12.5% is one eighth

explanation.surface: A survey note: the height has shifted from top to bottom by an eighth.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: moving the answer's top letter to the bottom gives the fraction, so the solver moves that fraction's final H up to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation is height above a reference level such as the sea.

clue.text: Concrete is securing link – these are the facts

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast within, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: concrete, actual
as written
a tie is a link or bond

explanation.surface: A builder explaining that concrete is what holds the link in place: those are the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' wants to be the building material; here it is the adjective meaning actual.
explanation.definitionFit: Realities are things that actually exist or are true, so the facts of a situation.

clue.text: Virgil, I admit, contains work from another poet

indicators.note: contains says the letters are held within the words before it

blocks.note: inside virgIL I ADmit

explanation.surface: A confession that Virgil's epic borrows from an earlier poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: Virgil's Aeneid draws heavily on Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic of the Trojan War, a poem by a poet other than Virgil.

clue.text: Delay yearly exercise ...

blocks.note: per annum, abbreviated p.a.
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A note about postponing an annual workout, leading on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to the next clue; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a short stop or hold-up, and to pause is to delay briefly.

clue.text: ... still producing interference

blocks.note: first meaning: motionless, unchanging
second meaning: crackling noise on a radio or TV signal

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: an annual workout delayed yet still causing disruption.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means unmoving as an adjective and, as a noun, electrical noise disrupting broadcast reception.

clue.text: Almost overwhelm gang? That's shocking

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to flood is to overwhelm
a ring of criminals is a gang

explanation.surface: A query about nearly being overrun by a gang of thugs, and how alarming that would be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' looks like a comment on the gang, but it is the definition, in the sense of knocking someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooring someone is staggering or astonishing them, as if knocking them to the ground, hence shocking.

clue.text: Mature reason that stops one revealing programme

indicators.note: stopping something cuts it short, so the word before loses its final letter

blocks.note: to age is to mature
an end is a purpose or reason
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A mature explanation that halts someone in the act of disclosing a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: the E of the first piece is lost, or shared with the second, as the reason cuts it short before the final one.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with at a meeting, a programme of business.

clue.text: Follower provides commercial gas lease

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
He, the symbol for helium
to lease is to rent

explanation.surface: A business notice about an advertisement for leasing a gas supply.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a supporter or disciple who sticks to a cause or leader.
